nodes.summary: The derivative of mean fitness with respect to the trait mean is `d/dμ w̄(μ) = 𝔼[(z - μ) W z] / v`, for bounded measurable fitness and `v > 0`.
nodes.title: Derivative of mean fitness with respect to the trait mean

nodes.summary: The gradient of mean fitness with respect to the vector of trait means is `∇_μ w̄(μ) = P⁻¹ 𝔼[W z · (z - μ)]`, for positive definite `P` and bounded measurable `W`.
nodes.title: Lande's gradient of mean fitness for multivariate traits

nodes.summary: Stein's lemma for the normal law `N(μ, v)`, `v > 0`: if `g` is differentiable with derivative `g'` and `g`, `(z - μ) g z` and `g'` are integrable, then `𝔼[(z - μ) g z] = v 𝔼[g' z]` (Stein 1981, Lemma 1).
nodes.title: Stein's lemma

nodes.summary: The mean fitness `w̄(μ) = 𝔼[W z]` of a population whose trait vector is distributed as `N(μ, P)`.
nodes.title: Mean fitness of a multivariate normal trait

nodes.summary: The mean fitness `w̄(μ) = 𝔼[W z]` of a population whose trait is distributed as `N(μ, v)`.
nodes.title: Mean fitness of a normally distributed trait

nodes.summary: The Lande–Arnold selection gradient for one normally distributed trait: for a differentiable bounded fitness function with integrable derivative, `β = S / v = 𝔼[W' z] / w̄`, the average slope of relative fitness `W / w̄` (Lande–Arnold 1983).
nodes.title: The Lande–Arnold selection gradient

nodes.summary: Lande's equation for one normally distributed trait (Lande 1979): the selection differential is the phenotypic variance times the derivative of log mean fitness with respect to the trait mean, `S = v · d/dμ log w̄(μ)`.
nodes.title: Lande's equation

nodes.summary: Lande's equation (Lande 1979): for a multivariate normal trait vector, the selection differential is the phenotypic covariance matrix applied to the gradient of log mean fitness with respect to the trait means, `S = P ∇_μ log w̄(μ)`.
nodes.title: Lande's equation

nodes.summary: The directional selection differential `S = 𝔼[W z · (z - μ)] / w̄` of a trait vector distributed as `N(μ, P)`: the fitness-weighted mean trait vector of the selected parents minus the mean `μ` before selection. If `w̄ = 0` it is the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: Multivariate directional selection differential

nodes.summary: The directional selection differential `S = 𝔼[(z - μ) W z] / w̄`: the mean trait of the selected parents, weighting each individual by its fitness, minus the mean trait `μ` before selection. If `w̄ = 0` the division returns the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: Directional selection differential

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
